conviction_note: Q3 revenue should clear a ~$69m bar on management's own disclosed $24m June run-rate (~$72m if held), but that run-rate is public, the Q2 revenue beat closed only +0.95% after a gap-down on EPS, and the call also has to update a deal now under an FTC Second Request and a standalone guide whose low end the June rate merely reaches; the findings therefore offset to an impact_sum of 0.0, while the scaled number is a mild lean, p_up 55 on a 7.5% absolute move (no usable option chain; name's median reaction 6.44%, max 10.28%), because the quarter itself is the most likely line to land first.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $68.56m and EPS $0.00 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MDXG/earnings/), $69.92m and EPS -$0.01 from 5 analysts (FXEmpire, https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/mdxg/earnings); two sources agreeing within 2%. Company guide: FY2026 net sales $260-290m standalone, adj. EBITDA approaching breakeven (Q2 release, https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/mimedx-announces-second-quarter-2026-operating-financial-results). H1 = $59m + $64.4m = $123.4m, so the guide implies H2 $136.6-166.6m (Q3+Q4 ~$68-83m each).
positioning_check: Short interest 9,264,529 shares, 6.52% of float, 9.1 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 record date (published by FINRA 2026-10-26), vs 9,362,899 / 6.6% / 7.35 days at 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MDXG/short-interest/). Elevated days-to-cover on thin turnover but not a crowded float; part of it is plausibly merger-arb hedging of the 0.4735 MDXG shares per Sanara share. No usable option chain (34 contracts of open interest, ATM legs not two-sided), so no skew; put/call OI 0.7. Tape: spot $3.95, -15.2% over 20 days, +5.6% over 5 days, -50% from 52-week high.

findings.finding: Management disclosed on the Q2 call that June 2026 net sales were $24m and that the June rate alone puts the year 'already within range'; three months at that rate is ~$72m for Q3, about 3-5% above the $68.6-69.9m consensus, with Wound volume +22% sequentially in Q2 and Surgical +15% y/y, and management also guiding gross margin to the 'mid-70s beginning in the third quarter' (from 69% GAAP / 73.7% adjusted in Q2) and no further significant bad-debt charges in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $64.36m beat a $63.46m consensus by 1.4% while EPS missed; stock gapped down 5.7% intraday and closed +0.95% (baseline). Q1 2026: revenue missed and FY guide was cut from $340-360m to $260-290m, yet the stock closed +8.74%. Q4 2025 print: -6.44%. Revenue beats on this name have not been paid much.
findings.why_not_priced: The June figure is in the call transcript, not the release, and a $72m run-rate sits above both published consensus figures ($68.56m, $69.92m); if the street had anchored on it, consensus would be at or above $72m rather than at a ~5% sequential step from Q2. Against that, the stock fell 15% over 20 days, so the market is not pricing an upside quarter.
findings.independence: Smith+Nephew's Q2 2026 report (2026-08-04) described sequential improvement in skin substitutes 'driven by hospitals', the channel MiMedx said grew fastest (https://prod-we-cm.smith-nephew.com/en/news/2026/08/04/second-quarter-2026-results). The margin and bad-debt statements share the same transcript and are merged here, not filed separately.

findings.finding: The standalone FY2026 guide of $260-290m is only reached at its low end by the disclosed June run-rate ($123.4m H1 + ~$144m H2 at $24m/month = ~$267m); the midpoint ($275m) needs H2 of ~$152m, so the call is more likely to narrow toward the low half or hold the range than to raise it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: guide cut by ~$75m at the midpoint and the stock closed +8.74% (relief); Q2 2026: guide reiterated, close +0.95%. This name has not punished guide cuts that clear uncertainty.
findings.why_not_priced: Arithmetic from public numbers; consensus revenue of ~$69m for Q3 already sits near the low half of the guide, so a narrowing to the low half is largely in the bar. If the market expected a raise, the stock would not be -50% from its high and -15% over 20 days.
findings.independence: Shares the June $24m figure with finding 1 (same transcript) but lands on a different line (the forward range, not the quarter); the June arithmetic is the only common input. No independent source for a full-year consensus was found.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-15 MiMedx and Sanara each received an FTC Second Request on the $350m Sanara merger, extending the HSR waiting period to 30 days after substantial compliance; management had said on the Q2 call the deal would close by year-end and that the 2027 combined outlook (>$400m revenue, >20% adj. EBITDA margin) assumes a 2026 close, so the call must now restate the timeline and probably the 2027 framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the 2026-10-16 disclosure MDXG fell about 2.8% and SMTI 5.5% (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/mi-medx-sanara-merger-faces-fresh-regulatory-obstacle-smti-stock-falls-below-this-key-support-level-for-the-first-time-in-4-months/cZxKJ0GRBsM). On the deal announcement day (Q2 print) the stock closed +0.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Second Request itself is public and was sold on the day; what is not yet known is management's revised close date and whether the 2027 >$400m outlook is withdrawn or re-based. Financing question answered: the $300m Hayfin term loan (SOFR+6.25%) buys Sanara, which its own forecasts put at $121m 2026E revenue and $21.5m adj. EBITDA (DEFM14A), i.e. an accretive surgical ramp, so a delay defers profit rather than relieving distress; MiMedx owes a $22.5m reverse fee only on a failure to close when required, and the outside date is 2027-07-29 extendable to 2028-01-29.
findings.independence: Sanara's DEFM14A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000714256/000121390026097669/ea0304447-01.htm) for the Sanara forecasts, outside date and fee; the timeline statement is from the Q2 call transcript (shared document with finding 1).

findings.finding: Integra LifeSciences' Q3 2026 release (2026-10-21) showed Wound Reconstruction revenue $81.5m, -2.9%, with declines in MicroMatrix (particulate) and Integra Skin offsetting growth in PriMatrix and DuraSorb, and called Tissue Reconstruction 'softer-than-expected'; a peer that reported after MiMedx last spoke shows soft hospital/surgical wound demand, though MicroMatrix weakness is also consistent with share loss to particulate competitors like MiMedx (domestic particulate +21% in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of MDXG reacting to Integra prints; proxy only.
findings.why_not_priced: Integra's wound business is mostly surgical/burn and not Medicare office-based skin substitutes, so few would read it across; its sign for MiMedx is ambiguous (category softness vs share shift), which is why it is sized small and near zero.
findings.independence: Proxy, not confirmed by MiMedx or a direct counterparty. No other Q3 wound peer (Organogenesis 2026-11-05, Smith+Nephew early November) has reported inside the window.

findings.finding: Short interest was 9.26m shares, 6.5% of float, 9.1 days to cover at 2026-10-15, up from 7.35 days at 2026-09-30 as volume fell, into a stock that is -15% over 20 days and +5.6% over the last 5; a clean beat on thin turnover has a covering mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (+8.74% on a guide cut) is the one print where relief overwhelmed the fundamentals; whether covering drove it is not documented.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not a fundamental the price absorbs ahead of the print; 6.5% of float is not crowded, and part is plausibly merger-arb hedge that does not cover on earnings, so this is small.

outside_window.finding: CMS CY2027 Physician Fee Schedule final rule, expected around 2026-10-31 to mid-November (the CY2026 rule came 2025-10-31); the proposed rule kept the ~$127/cm2 flat skin-substitute rate and moved non-sheet products to national pricing, and the CEO said CMS shows 'little interest in course correcting'. A final rule inside 2026-10-29 is possible but not expected.

Organogenesis, the largest pure-play skin-substitute peer, reports Q3 2026 on 2026-11-05 after the close (Q2 net product revenue $42.8m vs $100.8m a year earlier); its read-through lands after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The modest positive lean on the quarter cuts against a -15% 20-day run-up and a stock 50% off its high, which say the market expects little; with no option skew to read, the 5-day +5.6% bounce and 9-day cover suggest some positioning for relief, and the deal delay and low-end guide arithmetic pull the other way, so p_up is held at 55.
lessons_applied: nothing changed: the draft was already sized for the reaction function (rule 1, Q2 beat closed +0.95%), against a two-source bar inside the company guide (rule 6), with the financing question answered before signing the deal finding (rule 4), the peer proxy filed small (rule 5) and short interest checked before the negatives (rule 7)
